mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A reconditioned or rebuilt Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi engine typically costs between £2,000 and £5,000 for the supply-only unit, depending on the level of rebuild and upgrades included.
- Rebuilt units address common Puma-era failure points like EGR and turbo wear.
- Supply and fit packages are available through our specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of turbo failure in a Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi engine.
- Look for sudden loss of power, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, or the vehicle entering limp mode.
- A whining noise from the engine bay or visible oil leaks around the turbo housing are also strong indicators.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, given the rising classic car values, replacing the engine is often a sound financial decision.
- A typical 2007-2011 model is valued between £8,000 and £18,000+, making a £3,000-£5,000 rebuild a small percentage of the vehicle's worth.
- A rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty adds reliability and protects your investment.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi to a 2.2 TDCi engine?

acceptedAnswer.text:
While both are Puma-era engines, a direct swap is not straightforward.
- The 2.2 TDCi (DT224) requires different ECU mapping, wiring harnesses, and emissions components to function correctly.
- We recommend sticking to a like-for-like 244DT replacement to ensure guaranteed compatibility and MOT compliance.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi typically takes 2 to 3 days at a specialist workshop.
- This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly tested.
- Complex cases requiring additional fabrication or cooling system upgrades may take slightly longer.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the stretched 8-seat Defender 130 officially launched, it was exclusively powered by the robust 2.4-litre Puma diesel, designed to handle heavier payloads and towing duties while meeting Euro 4 emissions standards.

milestones.description: 244DT (2402cc), 122hp, launched as the first dedicated Defender 130 model, replacing modified 110 chassis stretch conversions with a factory-built heavy-duty variant.

Production of the 2.4 TDCi ceased, replaced by the 2.2 TDCi (DT224) to meet stricter Euro 5 emissions standards, though the 2.4 TDCi remains highly sought after for its relative mechanical simplicity.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi (244DT) is a proven workhorse engine, but its age and heavy-duty usage profile mean specific components are prone to wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbo Wastegate & Boost Loss - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi 244DT Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The vacuum-operated wastegate solenoid and actuator arms are prone to sticking or failing under heavy load, causing sudden power loss and triggering limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the faulty solenoid, vacuum lines, and actuator arm to restore boost control.
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if turbo internals are healthy and there is no shaft play.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if there is concurrent bottom-end wear, oil consumption, or turbo shaft failure.

problems.recommendation: If the engine is fundamentally sound, addressing the turbo wastegate and EGR system with a specialist clean and seal replacement is highly cost-effective. However, if the engine exhibits heavy oil consumption, knocking, or has exceeded 150,000 miles with a patchy service history, a full reconditioned replacement is the most reliable long-term solution for a heavy-duty Defender.

problems.group: EGR Cooler Fouling & Injector Seal Leaks
problems.h4: EGR Cooler Fouling & Injector Seal Leaks - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 2.4 TDCi 244DT Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Heavy commercial use and short journeys cause the EGR cooler to clog with carbon, while aging injector copper seals leak combustion gases, leading to black sludge buildup in the rocker cover.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removing and cleaning the EGR system, fitting an EGR blanking plate, and replacing all injector copper seals.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly cost-effective preventative maintenance if caught early before head damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if severe carbon buildup has caused chronic overheating or cylinder head damage.
